A bracket shape whose spine lies past the widened east edge, leaving a clip backtrack that splitBoundaryBacktracks still looks for on the exact tile edge.
A polygon 1% larger than tile 4/9/5, which fully covered the old clip rect but not the 5% widened one, so full-cover detection flips.
A polygon with an edge on lon 180 at tile 0/0/0, whose antimeridian vertices are no longer locked as boundary points during simplification.
An ocean at tile 1/1/1 with one island inside, one across the tile's north edge and one across the widened west edge.
A world ocean at tile 1/1/1 with islands inside and across the tile's west edge, checking outer and hole winding after the widened clip.
A full-world rectangle at zoom 0, whose lon 180 edges now sit inside the widened clip rect instead of on it.
A wedge crossing lon 45 up to zoom 4, where the batch fill now runs past the exact edge the outline stops at.
The donut and square across lon 0 up to zoom 1, so batch tile 1/0/0 can be compared with the single-tile path.
A world-covering polygon up to zoom 1, which can no longer fill the widened rect at the world edge, so full-cover tiles become tessellated.
A bracket shape up to zoom 4, whose clip backtrack now lands on the widened edge in the batch path.
A square crossing lon 0 up to zoom 1, checking that fill vertices in the overlap band keep the 6-float layout.
The same donut and square input as the sync call, whose async tile set should match it.
A polygon with one hole, which must yield one polygon part with 2 rings.
A closed Mercator rectangle ring, which must come back as a closed chain.

source.quote: keeps every island hole through compileSingleTile (none dropped or collapsed)

obligations.statement: For a large ocean polygon with several island holes, compileSingleTile at tile z=1 x=1 y=1 returns exactly one polygon that still contains every hole ring, none dropped or collapsed.

source.quote: holes wind opposite to the outer ring (not inverted → not filled over)

obligations.statement: For a large ocean polygon with island holes compiled at tile z=1 x=1 y=1, compileSingleTile returns a non-degenerate outer ring and every hole ring winds opposite to it.

source.quote: outline of a polygon spanning lon=45° tile boundary does NOT include the boundary segment
